## Historical audit — S0159

**Source:** `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-02/scene-rsi-rsi-1-3d-blender/outputs/scene_rsi_pilot/results/r1/sceneevolve_cli/C2/test/commons_199974832/trajectory.jsonl`. Only chunk 3 of 6 is visible; citations below refer to this file.

| Evidence | Observation and interpretation |
|---|---|
| Line 20, `model_request`, chars [0,302747) | The assigned goal was a separate-mesh reconstruction of one indoor RGB photograph, with matching camera, framing, materials and occlusion. The student interpreted it as an antique woodworking shop; that semantic description is the student’s observation, not an independently inspected image. |
| Line 20, student programs and runner results | The first program constructed multiple assets: walls, window, shelves, bench, planes, kettle, bottle, vise and bowl. Multipart assemblies include, for example, a plane body, blade and handles. It set object rotations, a 27 mm camera, three lights and procedural wood/metal materials. These are code-level evidence of intended pose, connections and textures, not proof of correct geometry or appearance. |
| Line 20, step 1 audit and revision | The student reported a gray cuboid obscuring the bowl, excessive side-shelf extent and washed-out materials. It hypothesized a Boolean/cutter problem, local shelf geometry and lighting respectively; it kept the camera fixed. The next complete program replaced the Boolean bowl with panels and rim, shortened shelf runs and reduced light powers. This was the student’s own prompted visual audit, not a teacher diagnosis. |
| Line 20, step 1 and 2 runner feedback | Both executions reported `ok: true`, finished 16 samples and saved render and blend files. This establishes technical render success, not visual fidelity or verified part contact. The student was provided image references, but their pixels are not visible in this audit. |
| Line 22, `model_response`, chars [0,22497) | The student chose `BEST 2` and reported remaining pale materials, regular shelf silhouettes and empty foreground strips. It supplied a full revised program using diffuse colors for shader initialization and darker finishes, varied shelf-plane heights and angles, and added tabletop clutter, while retaining the camera and lights. The proposed shader-default explanation remains a hypothesis. |
| Lines 23–24, `select` and `execute`, chars [0,59) and [0,22472) | Step 2 was recorded as fallback; step 3 was launched with the revised program. No step 3 result is visible in this chunk, so its execution outcome and final submission are unknown. |
| Line 21, `codex_session`, chars [0,4770) | The student session completed with zero tool calls; shell, browser, image-viewing tools and multi-agent operation were disabled. The visible process shows prompted iterative modeling, not independent filesystem or web exploration. |

**Teacher input and adoption:** No teacher message, detection, diagnosis or proposed update is visible here. The audit instructions and implementation request are runner/user prompts; the student’s own corrections were incorporated in subsequent code. No teacher receipt or adoption can be inferred.

**Outcome and lessons:** This is a technically successful pair of rendered builds followed by an execution with unknown result—not established overall scene success, algorithm failure, empty patch or technical interruption. Transferably, separate visual observations from causal hypotheses and preserve a rendered fallback when revising. The bowl-cutter and shader-color diagnoses, shelf extents, specific object identities and lighting levels are task-specific and unverified. Whether the shortened shelves left contents unsupported, the revised bowl’s parts actually connected, and step 3 improved framing, color or occlusion remain unresolved without the unseen render and results.
